subject: Runtime fit & token charter — Olive Labs onboarding
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Mendez <anna@olivelabs.com>; Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Runtime fit & initial model constraints for Olive Labs

Anna — thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, this thread is to capture the early model shortlist, context requirements, and a first-pass token estimate so CS and Eng can align on the implementation plan. I attached a quick token profile workbook and the implementation playbook (high level).

Summary of requirements (from discovery):
- Primary workload: customer support conversation summarization + intent classification + short synthesis for follow-ups.
- Typical user message: ~250 tokens; expected assistant response (summaries / SOT): ~800–1,200 tokens depending on context.
- Context window: need to retain up to last 8–10 customer messages plus metadata (roughly 6k–9k tokens for history).
- Latency SLO: P95 < 500 ms for text generation calls (interactive UI), occasional async jobs allowed to be slower.
- Security: standard SOC2 checklist in progress; procurement will need the security questionnaire filled.

First-pass traffic assumptions (please confirm):
- Peak concurrent active sessions: 200–300 (UI-heavy hours)
- Avg requests/day: 20k–25k (ramp to 30k within 3 months)
- Estimated tokens/month (generation + input): 18M–28M (spread across peak and off-peak). See attached token profile for scenario breakdown.

Model shortlist (initial candidates and rationale):
- LlamaX-13B-quant (recommended): good latency/cost balance at 8k context when quantized; best fit for deterministic summarization tasks.
- LlamaX-7B-quant (fallback / burst): lower-cost alternative for high concurrency windows; good for shorter-context answers.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (if accuracy for rare intents is insufficient): stronger on instruction-following for complex synthesis but will increase cost/latency — consider for small subset of heavier jobs.

Operational levers we propose to use: prefix caching for repeated system + prompt fragments, KV cache for long sessions to avoid re-sending full history on every request, and dynamic routing between 13B/7B based on request latency and budget.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Ben: validate the latency and concurrency sizing and give a POA for autoscaling/burst (due EOD 9/12).
2) Vivek: confirm whether KV cache profiles will support 8k windows for the 13B quantized runtime (due 9/13).
3) Anna / Javier: confirm procurement timeline + any additional security docs we should prep (please loop in procurement contact).
4) Lauren / Grace: schedule an implementation kickoff (30–45m) once contract is signed.

Attachments: olive_initial_token_profile.xlsx (tabbed scenarios), redwood_implementation_playbook_v1.pdf (high-level steps & responsibilities).

--

Thanks Lauren — this is great context. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Latency SLO: 500ms P95 is ideal for product; acceptable if warm-path responses occasionally go to ~700ms.
- Budget: we have an initial monthly budget target of ~$12k for hosted inference (may expand after Q1).

Lauren / team — did a quick sizing pass based on the workbook Lauren attached and Anna's clarifications. Key assumptions I used: average request tokens = 1,050 (250 in + 800 out); avg requests/day = 22k.

Sizing (initial):
- Monthly tokens: ~23.1M (22k * 1,050 * 30).
- Average QPS (sustained): ~0.26 QPS (22k/day spread) but burst windows push concurrent active sessions to 200–300 which drives higher short-term QPS (~6–8).
- Recommended baseline: 4 x A100-equivalent serving nodes running LlamaX-13B-quant with autoscale to 8 nodes on sustained bursts. This aims to hit P95 < 500ms for 8k context when using optimized kernels + batching.
- Cost-control: run a routing policy to send short-context requests to LlamaX-7B-quant; use prefix/KV caching to shave repeated tokens — likely net token reduction of 12–22% depending on prompt reuse.

Fallback plan: If P95 cannot be met in early tests, fall back to increasing concurrency with an emergency burst pool (best-effort) and consider a hybrid where heavy synthesis calls route to Falcon-40B-instruct asynchronously (non-blocking UX).

Deliverables I can produce by EOD 9/13:
- Node count and GPU type recommendation with projected cost (monthly)
- Autoscaling policy draft for bursts and steady-state
- Test plan for latency and end-to-end verification (including script for synthetic session replay)
